key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that surface smoothness is not a reliable proxy for optoelectronic quality.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics by suppressing non-radiative recombination and aging-induced electronic disorder.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium on 3D perovskites.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, and better preservation of optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract reports film-level improvements but does not establish device-efficiency gains or operational lifetime under real-world conditions.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
